title: How the game shows you yourself
target: What is driving the body and the view in Supermarket Simulator, so first-person settings are understood rather than guessed at.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A controller or keyboard and mouse

steps.do: Expect two controllers rather than one: the first-person view and the player character.
steps.because: the game keeps a first-person controller of its own and the player character has a controller of its own (FirstPersonController, PlayerController)

steps.do: Know that the body is posed rather than animated as one fixed piece.
steps.because: an IK handler poses the body rather than playing one fixed animation (PlayerIKHandler)

steps.do: Expect the surfaces you wear to be applied by their own controller.
steps.because: a skin controller applies the avatar's surfaces (PlayerSkinController)

steps.do: Let the game decide which device you are on, and expect the prompt to follow.
steps.because: input devices are handled by a manager of their own, with a kind of key display (InputDeviceManager, KeyDisplayType)

steps.do: Know that blinking is a system rather than a decoration.
steps.because: blinking is a system of its own, with a controller, a kind of blink and reasons for one (BlinkController, BlinkType, BlinkReasons)

steps.do: Change the view in one place, because the camera has its own controller and presets.
steps.because: the view is run by a camera controller of its own and camera setups can be kept as presets (CameraController, CameraPreset)

steps.do: Remember there is a camera that is not yours as well.
steps.because: there is a free camera of its own, separate from the one the player carries (FreeCamera)

steps.do: Expect a camera setting to be announced and answered rather than applied once.
steps.because: camera settings are invoked and listened for rather than applied in one place, and the picture is fitted to the screen by a fitter of its own (CameraSettingsInvoker, CameraSettingsListener, AspectRatioCameraFitter)

commonMistakes: Looking for one camera setting when the view, the presets and the free camera are separate.
Assuming the body you do not see is animating like a character in front of you.
Wondering why a prompt changed shape instead of reading it as a key-display kind.
Treating a screen-fit change as a gameplay setting.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
